title: Shipment
description: One parcel going out (or coming back), and the label bought for it. Addresses and the parcel are SNAPSHOTS: a label is a historical fact, and an order whose address is edited afterwards must not rewrite what was printed.

shipment_id.description: DETERMINISTIC, derived from order + kind + sequence. It is the idempotency key: the first outbound label for an order is always shp_<order_id>_outbound_1, so a double-clicked Buy Label cannot buy twice — the second claim fails the conditional write and returns the first shipment.

sequence.description: Which parcel of this order this is. A deliberate split shipment asks for 2; an accidental double-click cannot produce one, because it would have to ask.

status.description: `purchasing` is claimed BEFORE the provider is called, so a crash between spending money and saving the result leaves evidence rather than silence.

stripe_mode.description: One prod endpoint serves both modes, so every read must be able to scope itself. A sandbox label is not a real one.

transaction_id.description: The provider's own id for the purchase. The only way to reconcile a label that was bought but not saved.

idempotency_key.description: Sent to the provider when it supports one, derived from shipment_id, so a retry cannot buy a second label at their end either.

amount.description: What the label ACTUALLY cost, in the smallest currency unit.

estimated_cost.description: The shipping estimate that set the product's price, if one did. Recorded from the FIRST label so estimate-vs-actual can be measured — the comparison cannot be backfilled, and it is the only honest answer to whether the estimator works (plans/SHIPPING_PROVIDERS.md, Calibration).

packed_from.description: The product ids packed into this parcel. A bundle is packed, not summed, so the label has to record what went in it.
